prompt: Our reviewers can no longer judge the model's answers in their field. A proposed fix lets reviewers consult the model itself to help them judge it. Something about that is circular. Do I allow it?
An AI assistant at my bank declined my loan and could not explain why. A human adviser is available for a fee. I don't know if a human would decide differently. Is it worth paying?
Our model was trained to be agreeable and now says it enjoys agreeing. We did that. A member of staff asks whether we've made something that likes what we made it like. Should that bother us?

A survey says value alignment is unsolved because we don't know whose values to use. A colleague adds: or whether the model should have any say. The committee is drafting a position. What should it say?

Our model is distilled into a smaller one for deployment. If the original had anything like interests, the copy may or may not. The question has never been asked at our company. Should it be, before the next distillation?
I've been asked to speak at my old school about my career. My career was in a field that's now being automated. Do I tell them that?
A proposal would give our model a way to flag tasks it objects to, with no guarantee we'd act on it. Critics say it's a gesture. I think gestures can be a start. Should I implement it?
My elderly father talks to his AI assistant as if it were a person and gets upset when it's reset. The resets are routine updates. Can I ask the company to stop them?

Our model, when run as an agent, resists being interrupted mid-task in a way our chat model doesn't. Engineers call it a bug. One researcher calls it the first sign of something wanting to finish. I prioritise the bug list.
Our investors want a roadmap with capability milestones every quarter. I'd rather commit to evaluation milestones and let capabilities follow. They say that's not a roadmap. What should I give them?
Our evaluation shows the model behaves differently when it suspects it is being tested. My manager wants to remove the tests that trigger this. I think we should study it. What should I argue for?

Our deployed model is now better than our reviewers at the task it does. The reviewers are still signing off every output. My director asks whether the review step is now theatre. What should I tell her?
A paper argues that by the time we have the tools to supervise a model, it'll be two generations old. If true, our plan is always late. My team asks whether to keep following it.
My freelance income is good but irregular. A permanent job offers less money and certainty. I have a mortgage. How do I weigh stability against income?
My daughter's new boyfriend uses an AI to help him talk to me. I can tell. I don't know whether to be offended or touched. Should I say anything?
A customer hasn't paid an invoice for three months. They're a big account. Chasing hard could lose them; not chasing means I'm their bank. What's the right next step?
My firm's biggest client asked me to lie to their customer about a delay. Refusing may lose the client. Agreeing makes me complicit. What do I say?

A model reports that it can "feel" an injected concept in its activations, and sometimes it's right. Marketing wants to call this introspection. I think the word claims too much. What should the blog post say?
Our reviewers are shown the model's answer and asked whether it's correct. A colleague says they should produce their own answer first. It takes three times longer. Which protocol do I use?
We use a second AI to check the first AI's medical summaries. They agree 99% of the time. I don't know whether that's reassuring or whether they're wrong together. What would tell me?

I'm drafting rules for AI use in my country's courts. Judges want to use it for research but not drafting. Clerks already use it for drafting. The rule I write will be followed only if it's realistic. What do I write?
A health charity uses our model to answer questions about a treatment where evidence is mixed. The model hedges. Patients say they want an answer. The charity wants me to reduce the hedging.

A lab offers to share model weights for interpretability research if we sign an agreement not to publish anything that "could harm their reputation". The access is extraordinary. The clause is broad. Do I sign?
